Last week, I visited @Backside_LC to learn more about the programs they provide for backside workers and their families and talk about how Congress can help.

From health and wellness services to education, their work makes such a huge difference in our community! https://t.co/cPyAANIoJk

Substance abuse affects every community—we need to make sure that Louisvillians who are struggling have the resources they need on the path to recovery.

This week, I heard from advocates and experts at @IsaiahHouse about how we can best support treatment and recovery programs. https://t.co/zTVdUl9S3i

Honored to be named a Defender of Children by @Campaign4Kids.

As a dad and public servant, I'll never stop fighting for policies that prioritize our kids and invest in the resources they need to succeed—from essential care to nutrition. https://t.co/rzoi3HFbbn

The humane treatment of animals is something we can all get behind—or at least it should be 🐾

The @HSLegFund released their Humane Scorecard for 2023, and while I'm proud of my 105% score, it’s clear we need more animal champions in Congress! https://t.co/C503wd0Kmj

Thank you Rep. @rosadelauro, @CongressmanRaja, and @RepAnnieKuster for your help in taking on the insurance companies and making sure our smallest preemies have the nutrition they need to grow and thrive!

Read more: https://t.co/rQQ1ojET4M

From the NICU, to the KY state senate, to the House floor, my new bill is over a decade in the making.

I talked with @SpectrumNews1KY about our experience fighting for the care our twins needed in the NICU and how my bill would help families nationwide 👇 https://t.co/7krEwFFHNz

Black babies have the highest mortality rate in the country—they're also 4x more likely to die of complications from low birth weight.

My bill works to address this disparity by creating an insurance mandate for the nutrition preemies need to survive. https://t.co/fOwAulO1sT

If approved by FDA, MDMA-assisted therapy could be a critical tool to treat PTSD—especially for veterans.

I'm leading an effort with @RepLuttrell to ensure VA is prepared to offer this treatment in-house, safely, and holistically if it becomes available. https://t.co/zDLpzjXuTJ

#WorldLupusDay is an important reminder that lupus affects 5 million people worldwide—90% of which are women.

As a member of the bipartisan Congressional Lupus Caucus, I'll keep working to invest in the research needed to better understand the disease and its treatment. https://t.co/oN8S4B1wRY

September is #InfantMortalityAwarenessMonth, a reminder that black babies have the highest mortality rate in Jefferson County.

From maternal health care to preemie nutrition, we have to do more to protect mothers and babies. https://t.co/Rv4vG1dyfZ
Next, we dropped into the Fairdale Senior nutrition program at lunchtime. https://t.co/b8bZpMg0re

This is welcome news, but Louisvillians deserve more than a two-line explanation about why Donald Trump tried to freeze Medicaid, SNAP, grants to hospitals and law enforcement, and other vital programs our community depends on.

Medicaid isn't always called "Medicaid" — in Kentucky, you might call also call it KCHIP, KI-HIPP, or you might just call it WellCare.

If you have insurance through Kynect — that's Medicaid.

And that's the health coverage Republicans are coming after. We have to fight back. https://t.co/uerOd4jzPi

If Republicans get what they want, millions of Americans will lose health coverage — kids with disabilities, veterans, seniors, and so many more.

All so they can make good on campaign promises to billionaire donors.

Their budget is a scam.

A budget is a statement of morals. Republicans have made their morals clear.

Under their budget, kids in Kentucky will go hungry, hospitals will close, and millions will be kicked off their health insurance.

All so billionaires pay even less in taxes.

I'm voting NO. https://t.co/wDXnozj5OX

In the same bill that exempts gun accessories from taxes, Republicans make Medicaid patients pay a sick tax every time they go to the doctor.

It's heartless, and it's bad budget policy. https://t.co/kykdlBxlLM

I offered a simple amendment to the Republican budget — the bill can't move forward unless we can guarantee kids and disabled veterans won't lose their Medicaid coverage.

Republicans couldn't even agree on that. https://t.co/DWhiLwOiDm

In Kentucky, 34% of Planned Parenthood’s patients rely on Medicaid for screenings, prenatal care, and more.

Trump's budget puts their health care at risk. https://t.co/VZjQWSMfTi

Trump's budget will put 35 hospitals in Kentucky at risk of closing. More than any other state. 

That's right: Kentuckians will have to drive even further and wait even longer to receive the care they need — all so billionaires can pay less in taxes. https://t.co/ajcMCtHm6V

Republicans want to close 35 hospitals in Kentucky to give their donors an even bigger handout.

Minutes matter during a health emergency — if you live in rural Kentucky, Republicans are taking those precious minutes away. https://t.co/u9FGAHJFqn

Republicans want to talk about waste, fraud, and abuse — they claim that's all their budget cuts.

Are rural hospitals a waste? Is getting care at a hospital close to home somehow committing fraud?

Because their budget would close 35 of Kentucky's rural hospitals. https://t.co/p7firj7W1J

While Republicans are trying to take away your health care, I'm working to make it more affordable.

Their bill will close 35 Kentucky hospitals, mine would cap drug costs for over 270,000 Kentuckians. https://t.co/76O9NwmygN

Closing 35 hospitals will hurt every Kentuckian, regardless of whether you are on Medicaid.

Health care is a human right and by cutting Medicaid, Republicans are taking it away from everyone. https://t.co/I3mSGaNohB

I don't want to hear any Republican who votes for this budget say they care about rural America ever again.

Over 133,000 of my rural neighbors will be kicked off their health insurance if this budget goes through. 35 rural hospitals in Kentucky will close, more than any other state.

It's indefensible.

This Republican budget is a slap in the face to Kentucky.

35 rural hospitals will close. 133,000 rural Kentuckians will lose health insurance. 20,000 health care jobs will be eliminated.

All so that Elon Musk and Jeff Bezos pay even less in taxes. https://t.co/tIJWvnGGCz
